claims.wording: At a target risk of 20% with 95% confidence and a 20% acceptance floor, neither the QLoRA-adapted system nor the zero-shot baseline could be certified on RAMS: both are Infeasible, so no comparison of certified acceptance between them is possible.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS certification split, 1,396 source-document groups
claims.method: Joint finite-sample SCoRC certificate (arXiv 2606.08517 Thm 1) at alpha=0.20, delta=0.05 split three ways across systems, acceptance floor 0.20; conservative Hoeffding/Clopper-Pearson/Bonferroni audit as a descriptive cross-check.
limitations: H1 and H2 collapse to a single test when both baselines are infeasible; this is ONE finding, not two.
No numerical difference is computed against an infeasible baseline.
Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack and to in-domain RAMS.
claims.verified_by: conformalextract certify (immutable artifact, git-canonical sha256 71c0de3e); independent reviewer PASS 2026-07-22 (evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.certification.json)

claims.wording: The secondary confirmatory comparison against the few-shot baseline is likewise Infeasible on both sides.
claims.method: As CX-H1-PRIMARY; few-shot arm uses the frozen tenth-percentile confidence candidate.
limitations: Reported jointly with CX-H1-PRIMARY as one finding, never as an independent second confirmation.
A known harness defect depressed the few-shot arm's confidence score, but it could not affect this outcome: the comparison failed on the QA side, not the baseline side.

claims.wording: The infeasibility reflects a capability gap rather than a limitation of the certification method: with an unlimited threshold grid, no finite-sample penalty and oracle threshold selection, the adapted system could accept at most 2.0% of documents at 20% empirical error, against a required 20%.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS, oracle risk-coverage diagnostic on certification and development splits
claims.method: Oracle risk-coverage frontier over source-document groups via certification_run.risk_coverage_frontier, using the same aggregation, eligibility, loss and score as the certifier; no threshold is selected or certified.
limitations: A diagnostic, not a certificate: it selects no threshold and certifies nothing.
The same diagnostic on the development split gives 3.0%, so the conclusion reproduces out of sample.
claims.verified_by: conformalextract risk-coverage-diagnostic; reviewer re-derived 2.01% independently through the implementer's own aggregation, 2026-07-22

claims.wording: QLoRA adaptation produced a large improvement in grounding fidelity: 95.7% of the adapted system's outputs parse and ground to the source document, against 39.4% zero-shot and 68.1% few-shot, with ungrounded spans falling from 5,355 to 340.
claims.scope: software and in-domain extraction quality; 9,124 RAMS trigger frames per system
claims.method: conformalextract parse-predictions under the ADR 0006 first-object extraction policy, applied identically to all three systems; spans validated against source document tokens.
limitations: "Valid" means parseable and grounded, NOT correct: a span can point at real document text and still name the wrong entity or role.
This improvement did NOT translate into a certified selective guarantee (see CX-H1-PRIMARY); it must never be reported without that null attached.
Scoped to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.
claims.verified_by: conformalextract parse-predictions; reviewer reconciled the counts against an independent extraction measurement, 2026-07-21

claims.wording: On content-bearing frames the zero-shot baseline outperformed the few-shot one (3,550 against 3,330), and the few-shot arm emitted 63 times more empty frames, indicating that the two frozen demonstrations taught the model to abstain and to continue generating rather than to extract.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS, this demonstration set and prompt template only
claims.method: Content-bearing versus empty-frame breakdown required by reviewer condition C3 of ADR 0006.
limitations: Holds for these two frozen demonstrations, this template and this model; a demonstration set without an empty-gold exemplar might not reproduce it.
A missing stop sequence contributed to the continuation behaviour but not to the empty-frame rate.

claims.wording: The population base-risk ceiling is not a forecast of certifiability: it bounds what an oracle confidence score could achieve, and in this project it allowed 46.5% acceptance where the actual score delivered 2.0%. The empirical risk-coverage curve on development settles selective feasibility at no cost and without sealed data.
claims.method: Comparison of the (1-r)/(1-alpha) population ceiling against the oracle risk-coverage frontier on the same development split.
limitations: Recorded as a joint process failure: the ceiling was used as a forecast at three separate gates, by both the implementer and the independent reviewer, and the free check was run by neither until after the sealed split was opened.
claims.verified_by: reviewer computed the development frontier independently and required the lesson be recorded naming both parties, 2026-07-22

claims.wording: Grounding fidelity and certifiability are orthogonal for grounded event-argument extraction on RAMS: the QLoRA adapter's ~16x grounding gain over the baselines moved the certifiable frontier by 0.017 for itself and by 0.000 for both baselines, because 87% of its remaining loss is grounded, well-formed, content-bearing output that names the wrong entity.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS certification split, 1,396 source-document groups, frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack
claims.method: Document loss decomposed into four channels (structural failure, grounding failure, valid-but-contentless, valid content-bearing); group-level channel contributions sum exactly to the unweighted mean of group means the certificate bounds under ADR 0009. Counterfactual: each system re-scored over content-bearing documents only, coverage measured against the restricted population. For the baselines the conclusion rests on an arithmetic ceiling rather than the counterfactual: accepting a fraction c at risk alpha requires population mean loss at most alpha*c + (1-c) = 0.84, and their restricted mean losses are 0.984 and 0.951.
limitations: Descriptive only: the decomposition and the grounding-oracle counterfactual select no threshold and certify nothing.
Conditional coverage under the grounding oracle is not a deployable acceptance rate and is not comparable across systems; the restricted population differs per system.

The restriction is NOT uniformly generous: it raises the loss of 24 few-shot and 21 QLoRA groups, and a correctness-oracle variant moves the baselines off zero. The baselines' result is carried by the arithmetic ceiling, not by the counterfactual.
The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short of the floor.
Scoped to in-domain RAMS under span-exact matching and to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack (86.3% parsed-output parity); portability is not established.
The certificate bounds average within-group loss, not the absence of error in any document (ADR 0009).
claims.verified_by: evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json (independent review, 2026-07-22: numbers CONFIRMED by from-scratch recomputation; BLOCK on six discipline/wording items, all corrected)

claims.wording: On the oracle risk-coverage curve, the 20% acceptance floor first becomes reachable at a target risk of about 0.406 for the QLoRA system, 0.930 for few-shot and 0.981 for zero-shot. Across the whole range below those points no selective policy at any threshold could have cleared the floor, so the infeasibility at the frozen 0.20 target is not an artefact of that particular choice; it holds across everything up to twice it.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS certification split, 1,396 source-document groups; oracle upper bound (the development split is reported in the same artifact and agrees, at 0.383 for the QLoRA system)
claims.method: The oracle risk-coverage curve carries no target risk; max acceptance at a given target is that fixed curve read at one height. No certificate is issued at any point on the curve; the frozen target of 0.20 is unchanged (ADR 0007).
limitations: An oracle upper bound with no finite-sample penalty, no grid and no multiplicity correction: usable only to rule operating points out, never to indicate that a weaker one would certify.

The crossing is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. A certificate at 0.406 would not issue: at the ~280 groups a 20% acceptance implies, the Hoeffding radius alone is 0.086 to 0.103 depending on allocation, putting the risk upper bound near 0.49 to 0.51.
Not comparable with the certification rates prior work reports at its own operating points, which are achieved certifications rather than oracle necessary conditions.

The verdict IS operating-point dependent above the crossing: oracle acceptance for the QLoRA system reaches 0.187 at a target risk of 0.40 and 0.316 at 0.45. The claim is that the frozen target is not a specially unlucky choice, not that no operating point behaves differently.
The frozen headline target remains 0.20 and no certificate exists at any other point.
Scoped to in-domain RAMS and the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.
claims.verified_by: evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json (independent review, 2026-07-22: curve-vs-committed-diagnostic equality and alpha_star inverse CONFIRMED by from-scratch reimplementation and 20,000 randomised trials)
